name: The Teen Idles
label: Dischord
lede: Four kids from Wilson High, one Greyhound trip to California, six hundred dollars in savings, and a thousand hand-glued sleeves that became Dischord No. 1.

eras.title: The Cramps did it
eras.text: D.C. punk in early 1979 was a handful of shows and a handful of kids. A few of those kids went to Woodrow Wilson High School, saw one gig that rewired them, and started a band before they could legally get into most of the clubs.

q: The first show that made us want to be in a band
years.h: The Cramps at the Hall of Nations
years.p: [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and [[Jeff Nelson|51f7994c-949d-4dbe-89eb-2c33f42a5620]] see [[The Cramps|96c1edac-1011-4cb8-882c-27248de35071]] at Georgetown's Hall of Nations. It's the night they decide to be in a band.
years.xp: MacKaye later said that until then, Ted Nugent was about as wild as music got for him. The Cramps ended that.

years.p: MacKaye on bass, Nelson on drums, [[Geordie Grindle|2f8ebbdb-3b57-4648-a339-bedf27b86ab3]] on guitar and Mark Sullivan singing, all out of Wilson High.

Sullivan goes off to school. MacKaye's friend Henry Garfield, later [[Henry Rollins|656b39fb-979c-4c57-bb87-61d1a8eb38d1]], can't take the spot, so [[Nathan Strejcek|b53e7b75-696d-43f5-98ff-bc3d104e0d74]] steps in.

years.h: The Slinkees become the Teen Idles
years.p: New singer, new name. The lineup that makes Dischord No. 1 is set.

eras.title: Too young to rock, too loud to stop
eras.text: The Teen Idles lived about a year and a half, and 1980 was nearly all of it. They chased the Bad Brains, got thrown out of clubs for being underage, took a bus across the country, and came back with the idea that would outlast them: an X on the back of the hand.

years.h: Kicked out of clubs, to their delight
years.p: Many in the band and its crowd are under 18. The Bad Brains are, as Dischord puts it, maybe the greatest band in the world in 1980, and the Teen Idles want to be where they play. Clubs keep showing them the door.

years.h: Two demos, and a room full of laughter
years.p: The band tapes two demo sessions at a local studio. Members remember the engineer and a visiting band laughing at them while they played.

years.cap: The Teen Idles in California, August 1980
years.h: Greyhound to California, and the X comes home
years.p: The band rides the bus west with roadies Sullivan and Garfield, the "fifth Idle." At San Francisco's Mabuhay Gardens, the underage kids get a marker X on their hands so the bar knows not to serve them.
years.xp:
Back in D.C., the band pitched the same system to local clubs: mark the kids, let them in. The 9:30 Club adopted it.

A few months later an X-marked pair of hands, belonging to MacKaye's younger brother [[Alec MacKaye|bb05a948-ea44-4c9b-9d19-2a48f757ca22]], was on the cover of Minor Disturbance. The X would come to stand for straight edge.

q: Let's give it 100 percent, for a minute and a half
years.h: Eight songs in Don Zientara's house
years.p: The EP is cut at Inner Ear, then a four-track in [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]]'s Arlington home, with [[Skip Groff|8c4d8d50-a6a7-4fa6-9524-6e9c595816c1]] producing. Zientara remembered a band going flat out for ninety seconds at a time.
years.xp: Zientara described the Teen Idles as them against the world, playing every song as if they'd collapse at the end of it.

years.p: The band and a crowd of friends pose outside the Chancery in Washington. Jay Rabinowitz's photo becomes the back cover.
Grindle leaves after clashing with Nelson over religion. Without him, the band is finished.

years.h: Last show: opening for SVT at the 9:30 Club
years.p: The Teen Idles play their final set at the 9:30 Club. Too Young to Rock is taped live that night and goes straight onto the record.

Eight songs, about nine minutes. The band's $600 in savings pays for 1,000 copies, and Nelson, MacKaye, Strejcek and friends cut, fold and glue the sleeves by hand. The label they invent to put it out is called Dischord.
years.xp:
Nelson designed the cover around Susie Josephson's photo of Alec MacKaye's crossed, X-marked hands. The back cover is the Chancery crowd from Halloween.

Dischord's own history puts it simply: the members used the band's savings to document their music, and that became the first Dischord release.

years.p: MacKaye moves from bass to the microphone, Nelson stays on drums, and the next band starts almost immediately.

eras.title: What six hundred dollars built
eras.text: The Teen Idles were gone, but Dischord No. 1 kept doing its job. The label released its friends' bands one 7-inch at a time, the fifth Idle went national, and the EP stayed in print by riding along with the records it made possible.

years.p: Henry Garfield, roadie on the California trip, leaves D.C. to front Black Flag as Henry Rollins.
Teen Idles tracks land on Dischord No. 7, the compilation that mapped early D.C. hardcore.
With the original pressing long gone, the EP is gathered onto an LP with other early Dischord singles.

eras.title: Dischord No. 100 looks back at No. 1
eras.text: Fifteen years on, Dischord had outlived nearly every band it started with. When the catalog hit triple digits, the label went back to the very beginning.

years.p: The EP gets its first compact disc release.
For its hundredth release, Dischord puts out the February and April 1980 demos, the sessions where the studio laughed at them.
